doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: Armstrong, the boats and the downtown halls
title: Tom Albert's last time playing with Louis Armstrong, 1920s
summary: Tom recalls a job in the 1920s with Allen, Louis Armstrong and three cornets at Craig Church in Algiers, which was the last time he played with Armstrong before he went to Chicago.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: I played with Allen. I played with Allen, and I played, uh, in Allen with, uh, me and, uh, Lewis, Lewis Armstrong, Allen, and Three Cornets. Yeah, well, that's in the 20s.

Yeah. Yeah. When we went over and played the cornerstone lane in the way, uh, uh, Luch's mother's house there. Yeah. In the Jack, Ron Jack, what's the name of that place? That was, uh, wait, no, that was, uh, Craig Church. Craig Church, yeah. Craig Church. In Algiers over there.
That was the last time I played with Lewis Armstrong. Mm-hmm.
Yeah. And then he went to Chicago, I guess.
